summary: TechCrunch's Week in Review for early October 2023 rounds up the week's top tech stories. Highlights include Sam Altman backing a teen-founded AI startup, Google's hardware event and the Pixel 8 Pro, turmoil at Flexport, the Sam Bankman-Fried trial, Gmail's new bulk-sender rules, TikTok's ad-free tier test, and LinkedIn's AI tools. It also covers TechCrunch podcasts and TC+ reports.
one_line: TechCrunch's Week in Review covers Altman-backed Induced AI, Google's Pixel 8 launch, Flexport turmoil, the SBF trial, Gmail anti-spam rules, TikTok's ad-free test and LinkedIn AI.
key_facts: Sam Altman is among the backers of Induced AI, an AI startup founded this year by two teenagers that converts plain-English back-office task instructions into pseudo-code in real time.
Google's annual hardware event included updates on the Pixel 8, Pixel 8 Pro, Pixel Fold, Android 14, Pixel Buds, Google Assistant, Bard and Pixel Watch 2.

Darrell found the Pixel 8 Pro very similar to the Pixel 7 Pro but judged the improved cameras, brighter screen and enhanced AI features enough of an upgrade, apart from an underutilized temperature sensor.
Dave Clark, a former Amazon executive ousted as Flexport CEO after a year, called recent reporting on the company 'deeply concerning' in a post on X; Flexport is valued at $8 billion.
A book by Michael Lewis, 'Going Infinite,' debuted on the first day of the Sam Bankman-Fried trial and describes SBF's attempt to buy off Trump so he would not run for president again.
Starting next year, Gmail will require bulk senders to authenticate emails, offer an easy way to unsubscribe and stay under a reported spam threshold.
TikTok is testing a $4.99 ad-free subscription tier in a single English-speaking market outside the U.S.
LinkedIn unveiled AI features including an updated Recruiter platform, an AI-powered LinkedIn Learning coach and an AI tool for marketing campaigns.
Elon Musk said in September that X users create 100 million to 200 million posts daily excluding retweets, while X CEO Linda Yaccarino claimed 500 million posts per day.

IronNet, a cybersecurity startup founded in 2014 by retired four-star general Keith Alexander, shut down and laid off its remaining staff after raising more than $400 million and going public in August 2021.
At the SBF trial, the prosecution portrayed Bankman-Fried as knowingly committing fraud for wealth, power and influence, while the defense said he acted in good faith and got in over his head.
Breathe Battery Technologies has developed software that can be added to nearly any lithium-ion battery to give faster charging or greater longevity.
Fearless Fund, a firm founded to invest in women of color, is being barred from awarding grants to Black women founders.
